title: Win10 Became immune to awake after July 2026 Update
author: gab81

judgment.rationale: The report links crashes to low-power states on a machine with a known WHEA condition, but the current issue still does not show whether Awake was actively configured and running at the time of the 0.101 recurrence or provide a fresh diagnostic correlated with the crash.
evidence: The reporter says the machine crashes in balanced mode because of an existing low-power/WHEA condition and that VLC loop playback is an external workaround.
The reporter later confirmed the same problem on PowerToys v0.101.2323.0.
The only attached bug report predates that later recurrence.
The issue discussion still does not record the exact Awake mode or active-state signal during the failing session.
judgment.recommended_action: Request current Awake mode, a fresh diagnostic ZIP, and the matching WHEA event instead of guessing whether this is an Awake failure or the underlying hardware condition.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys fix cannot be chosen yet because the current report does not distinguish an Awake state/configuration problem from the machine's known low-power hardware or OS failure condition.

issue_context.summary: A Windows 10 system with a known low-power/WHEA problem reportedly crashes again after July 2026 updates even while Awake is expected to keep it active.
known_information: The reporter says VLC loop playback is an alternative workaround that keeps the system from crashing.
The report was updated to say the issue still occurs on PowerToys 0.101.2323.0.
The machine is an Asus Zenbook on Windows 10 22H2.
inferences: Awake may no longer be active in the same way after the update, but the current issue does not prove that the crash occurred while the configured Awake mode was truly engaged.
The underlying WHEA condition could also still be the direct failure and merely correlate with idleness.
issue_context.analysis: The decision is blocked on current, time-correlated Awake state and WHEA evidence, not on a lack of general discussion or historical context.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body, the follow-up comment, attached-report reference, labels, and timeline.
Noted that the attached diagnostic is from July and therefore predates the later 0.101 recurrence the reporter wants fixed.
Kept the outcome as needs-information rather than dismissing it, because the report still claims Awake previously masked the same low-power failure.

information_gaps.information: The exact Awake mode and whether Awake still showed as active immediately before the crash.

information_gaps.how_to_collect: Before reproducing, note the selected Awake mode/duration and include a screenshot or description showing the active state.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys diagnostic ZIP from the 0.101 recurrence.
information_gaps.why_needed: The current attachment predates the recurrence and cannot show the active module state or logs for the new failure.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Immediately after reproducing, add a comment containing /bugreport so the generated ZIP captures the current logs.

information_gaps.information: The matching WHEA-Logger event timestamp, Event ID, and General-tab details for the same crash.
information_gaps.why_needed: The WHEA event is needed to correlate the system crash with the claimed Awake failure window.

actions.label: Request current Awake crash evidence

comment.body:
Thanks for confirming that the problem still occurs on PowerToys 0.101.2323.0. The remaining blocker is that the attached report predates that recurrence, and the current thread still does not show whether Awake was actively holding the machine awake at the time of the crash.

**Needed**
1. Please note the exact Awake mode and whether Awake still showed as active immediately before the crash.
2. Immediately after another recurrence, please add a comment containing `/bugreport` so the generated ZIP captures the current PowerToys logs.
3. Please include the timestamp, Event ID, and General-tab text of the matching WHEA-Logger Event Viewer entry.

This will distinguish an Awake execution-state problem from the machine's existing low-power/WHEA condition.
